newsitem.title: BRAZIL: RESEARCH ALERT-Cemig maintained as buy.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT-Cemig maintained as buy.

text.p: Salomon Brothers said Thursday it reiterated its buy recommendation on Brazilian state-owned power firm Cemig after the release of second-half results.

-- "We reiterate our buy recommendation on the shares at this point based on the company's stronger earnings growth prospects in the medium term relative to most other Brazilian utilities," Salomon said in a report.
-- The growth was expected to be provided by the company's new foreign strategic partner, it said.
-- Cemig's first-half net profit of 89 million reais, equal to $82.7 million, or $0.64 per American Depositary Share (ADS), was in line with its estimate of 92 million reais, Salomon said.

-- Second-quarter net income totalled 62.3 million reais "was significantly higher than the first quarter's 26.7 million reais, largely owing to the effect of the company's 9.7 percent average tariff increase."
-- The rate increase took effect in April.
-- The cost of Cemig's energy purchases rose sharply in the last quarter due to an increase in wholesale tariffs to generators accompanying the tariff rise, Salomon said.
-- Wage increases and a rise in contributions to employee pension funds pushed the company's personnel expenses higher, it said.
-- Moreover, net margins also rose in the last quarter due mostly to a 5.7 million real charge steming from its voluntary retirement program.
-- Cemig common dropped 3.57 percent to 51 reais, while its preferred fell 0.5 percent to 56.20 reais at 1643 local/1543 edt in Sao Paulo.
